description: RemoteNodeHint bounded propagation: hopCount ≤ MAX_HINT_HOPS (3), timestamp within MAX_HINT_FRESHNESS_SECONDS (3600) of `now`. A hint that exceeds either bound is REJECTED by verifyRemoteNodeHint even if its reporter signature is still valid. This vector exercises the hintToHex canonical serialization plus the two propagation-limit rejection paths.

sharedKeys.note: Public key only — no secret-key material is committed. The reporter keypair was derived from a fixed 32-byte test seed inside the generator script for byte stability.

vectors.name: valid-propagation
vectors.description: Genuine RemoteNodeHint with hopCount=1 and timestamp=referenceNow. hintToHex produces the canonical CBOR serialization (integer-keyed map per ADR-0004). verifyRemoteNodeHint returns ok.

vectors.name: hop-count-exceeds-max
vectors.description: A hint is created at hopCount=MAX_HINT_HOPS (3, the maximum createRemoteNodeHint accepts) and then mutated post-hoc to hopCount=4 (MAX_HINT_HOPS + 1). The brand is preserved so verifyRemoteNodeHint treats the mutated object as a RemoteNodeHint and runs the verification path. The hopCount check rejects: 'hopCount 4 exceeds max 3'.

vectors.name: stale-hint
vectors.description: A genuine hint is created at timestamp=referenceNow, then mutated post-hoc to timestamp=referenceNow - MAX_HINT_FRESHNESS_SECONDS - 60 (3660 seconds in the past). The brand is preserved, so verifyRemoteNodeHint runs the freshness check, which rejects: 'hint outside freshness window'.

verification: Reference implementation: reference/topology/remote-node-hint.ts — createRemoteNodeHint, hintToHex, verifyRemoteNodeHint, MAX_HINT_HOPS, MAX_HINT_FRESHNESS_SECONDS.
notes: The hop-overflow and stale-timestamp mutations are constructed by spreading a genuine RemoteNodeHint and overriding a single field. The __brand field is preserved so verifyRemoteNodeHint still treats the mutated object as a RemoteNodeHint — this exercises the runtime verification path, not the constructor's input validation. This complements V-HINT-001 (which covers signature tampering and expired-timestamp mutations).
